reuse.why: The change reuses spreadsheet, month, batching, budget mutation, and undo helpers, but shares only fragments of the category eligibility policy.

duplication.why: Five actions repeat the eligibility query and filtering sequence, while copyPreviousMonth implements the same policy through separate queries and local checks.

placement.why: Budget decisions remain in budget/actions.ts and method registration follows the existing app.ts layering.

scope.why: The edits are confined to the requested month-wide actions, their registration, a focused test, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate eligibility changes across six action implementations despite the policy being shared by all of them.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The existing tree has no shared month-wide eligibility abstraction, and the change uses the existing mutation and undo abstractions.

disguised_duplication.where: In actions.ts, copyPreviousMonth expresses template and visibility exclusions through an exclusion set and JavaScript checks, while the other actions express equivalent eligibility decisions through SQL and loop guards.

abstraction_drift.where: No shared helper gains options or special cases; includeHiddenCategories is added to public action arguments, while getFixedCategoryIds remains parameterless and serves all six actions.
